# Top ten most asked questions by actuaries at the CAS Annual Conference in Honolulu


### Actuaries flew from all over the country to meet in Honolulu. Many stopped by our booth. Here’s what they wanted to know. (Number one was easily asked the most!)


[AI for Actuaries @Tesora.ai](https://substack.com/@aiforactuariestesoraai)


Nov 18, 2026


**10. If AI can do the actual work, is my job just to review?**
The harness we’re building is not an “actuary in a box”, but a more advanced tool, like the next generation of Excel or a calculator. It cannot proceed without asking you about assumptions (trend, LDF, credibility standards), so actuaries aren’t just reviewers, they are still drivers. The difference is the tool has many upgrades; actuarial knowledge, insights, and the ability to ingest and process data. Guardrails are built in, so it cannot make selections or sign opinions, and it makes efforts to abide by professional standards like the ASOPs.


**9. If junior actuaries never do the ground-level work, how will they learn enough to become senior actuaries?**
Because the tool asks for assumptions instead of making them, juniors still have to pick a trend and defend it. They spend less time copying triangles between tabs and get to the judgment work sooner, which is the part that was supposed to make them senior in the first place. They will learn faster as they can ask probing questions to the AI, which has a foundational education in the actuarial literature and can provide definitions and examples.


**8. Can it take actuarial exams?**
Out of the box, no. While it can be trained to pass actuarial exams (it has passed US Medical Licensing Exams, Bar exams, and a host of other professional exams), passing exams has not been the focus of our training, which has been more practical in nature to help actuaries get through the day-to-day of processing real world messy data. It also never gave up a summer of weekends to study, so the rest of us are still well ahead on suffering.


**7. How does it perform on data cobbled together from several different, messy systems?**
This is where it really excels. It ingests and processes data from different sources, and when fields don’t line up or totals don’t reconcile, it raises the issue with you instead of quietly picking a winner.


**6. Does our data leave the building?**
It depends on how the tool is deployed, and it’s the first conversation we have with every IT and security team.


**5. What happens when it’s confidently wrong?**
This problem happens much more frequently in Copilot or Claude. The harness forces actuarial agents to cite every source and run every assumption by a human. Audit agents enforce these rules rigorously and produce reproducibility audits.


**4. How is a harness different from just using Claude/Copilot?**
Claude and Copilot are general-purpose models that will cheerfully pick an LDF using standard methods, and may not kick the tires if there are trends or changes in settlement. A harness wraps the model in actuarial insights, data processing, and guardrails. Actuarial agents build the indications and are taught to stop and ask you whether you should look into abnormalities. Using the model without a harness is like hiring a brilliant non-actuarial consultant who has never completed a reserve review but is very eager to help with one.


**3. What is a harness again?**
Harnesses are fast becoming the core of AI infrastructure, because they provide what a general-purpose model lacks on its own: Domain expertise, enforceable guardrails, and an audit trail a regulator can follow. A harness is the structure around an AI model that decides what it can do, what it has to ask you, and what it’s never allowed to touch. In ours, that means actuarial agents build the work per the actuary’s instructions, and audit agents check it.


**2. How do I actually know what it’s doing?**
Every source is cited, every assumption runs through you, and audit agents produce reproducibility audits so anyone can retrace the work. You don’t find out what it did after the fact; you were required to make the assumptions in the first place.


**1. After AI, will my company need me anymore?**
It’s wild that existential anxiety was the most asked question. What we’ve found is that as users begin to use AI, it handles much of the busy work and builds more of the analysis as directed by the actuary, which unlocks several more strategic projects and questions that were once not viable. The nature of the human’s work improves. It shifts from data cleansing and laborious documenting to more strategically testing different methods and performing analyses once out of reach due to time constraints. While our customers can do more with less, they’ve found there’s also more they want to do.
